title.en: Volume 143 Biographies 93: Li Huaixian, Zhu Tao, Liu Peng, Cheng Rihua, Li Quanlue
title.raw: 卷一百四十三 列傳第九十三: 李懷仙 朱滔 劉怦 程日華 李全略 Volume 143 Biographies 93: Li Huaixian, Zhu Tao, Liu Peng, Cheng Rihua, Li Quanlue

sentences.zh: 李懷仙，柳城胡人也。

translations.literal: Li Huaixian was a man of the Hu people of Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaixian was a Hu from Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 世事契丹，降將，守營州。

translations.literal: He served the Khitan in his generation, was a surrendered general, and guarded Ying prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In his time he served the Khitan; a surrendered general, he held Ying prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祿山之叛，懷仙以裨將從陷河洛。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, Huaixian followed as a staff officer and took part in capturing the He and Luo regions.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Huaixian followed as a staff officer and helped capture the He and Luo regions.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒敗，又事史思明。

translations.literal: When An Qingxu was defeated, he again served Shi Siming.
translations.idiomatic: After An Qingxu was defeated, he served Shi Siming.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，有智數。

translations.literal: He was skilled at mounted archery and possessed resourcefulness.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in mounted archery and shrewd in counsel.

sentences.zh: 朝義時，偽授為燕京留守、范陽尹。

translations.literal: Under Chaoyi he was falsely appointed acting garrison commander of Yanjing and governor of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shi Chaoyi he was falsely appointed acting garrison commander of Yanjing and governor of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，元帥雍王統回紇諸兵收復東都，朝義渡河北走，乃令副元帥仆固懷恩率兵追之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, the commander-in-chief Prince of Yong led Huige and other troops to recover the Eastern Capital; Chaoyi crossed the Yellow River and fled north, whereupon the deputy commander-in-chief Pugu Huaien was ordered to lead troops in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 1, the Prince of Yong as commander-in-chief led Huige and allied forces to recover the Eastern Capital; Chaoyi fled north across the Yellow River, and the deputy commander Pugu Huaien was sent in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 時群兇瓦解，國威方振，賊黨聞懷恩至，望風納款。

translations.literal: At that time the remaining rebels were breaking apart and imperial prestige was rising; when the rebels heard Huaien was coming, they submitted at the sight of his banners.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel remnant was collapsing and imperial prestige was rising; at word of Huaien's approach, rebel bands surrendered.

sentences.zh: 朝義以余孽數千奔范陽，懷仙誘而擒之，斬首來獻。

translations.literal: Chaoyi fled to Fanyang with several thousand survivors; Huaixian lured and captured him, beheaded him, and presented the head as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi fled to Fanyang with a few thousand survivors; Huaixian lured him in, seized him, beheaded him, and sent the head to court.

sentences.zh: 屬懷恩私欲樹黨以固兵權，乃保薦懷仙可用。

translations.literal: Because Huaien privately wished to build a faction to secure military power, he strongly recommended Huaixian as usable.
translations.idiomatic: Huaien, seeking to build a faction to secure his military power, strongly recommended Huaixian.

sentences.zh: 代宗復授幽州大都督府長史、檢校侍中、幽州盧龍等軍節度使，與賊將薛嵩、田承嗣、張忠誌等分河朔而帥之。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong again appointed Huaixian chief administrator of the Youzhou metropolitan prefecture, acting chief minister, and military governor of Youzhou and the Lulong armies, and with the rebel generals Xue Song, Tian Chengsi, and Zhang Zhongzhi divided the Hebei region among them as commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong reappointed Huaixian chief administrator of Youzhou, acting chief minister, and military governor of Youzhou and Lulong, and with rebel generals Xue Song, Tian Chengsi, and Zhang Zhongzhi divided Hebei among them as regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 既而懷恩叛逆，西蕃入寇，朝廷多故，懷仙等四將各招合遺孽，治兵繕邑；

translations.literal: Soon after, Huaien rebelled, the western tribes raided, and the court had many troubles; Huaixian and the other four generals each gathered surviving rebels, drilled troops, and repaired towns;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huaien rebelled, western tribes invaded, and the court was beset by troubles; Huaixian and the other four generals each rallied surviving rebels, drilled troops, and rebuilt their districts;

sentences.zh: 部下各數萬勁兵，文武將吏，擅自署置；

translations.literal: each had tens of thousands of crack troops under him, and civil and military officers and officials were appointed on their own authority;
translations.idiomatic: each commanded tens of thousands of crack troops and appointed civil and military officers at will;

sentences.zh: 貢賦不入於朝廷，雖稱籓臣，實非王臣也。

translations.literal: tribute and taxes did not enter the court; though they called themselves vassals, in truth they were not the emperor's ministers.
translations.idiomatic: tribute and taxes never reached court; though they styled themselves vassals, they were not truly imperial subjects.

sentences.zh: 朝廷初集，姑務懷安，以是不能制。

translations.literal: The court had only recently been restored and for the moment pursued appeasement, and so could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: The newly restored court pursued appeasement for the moment and could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 懷仙大歷三年為其麾下兵馬使硃希彩所殺。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali, Huaixian was killed by Zhu Xicai, the army and horse commissioner under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 3, Huaixian was killed by his army and horse commissioner Zhu Xicai.

sentences.zh: 希彩自稱留後。

translations.literal: Xicai styled himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Xicai declared himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 恆州節度使張忠誌以懷仙世舊，無辜覆族，遣將率眾討之；

translations.literal: The Hengzhou military governor Zhang Zhongzhi, because Huaixian was an old associate, and that his clan had been destroyed without cause, sent a general at the head of troops to attack him;
translations.idiomatic: Hengzhou governor Zhang Zhongzhi, citing old ties with Huaixian and the unjust destruction of his clan, sent troops to attack Xicai;

sentences.zh: 為希彩所敗。

translations.literal: and was defeated by Xicai.
translations.idiomatic: and was defeated by Xicai.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不獲已，宥之。

translations.literal: The court, unable to do otherwise, pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to do otherwise, the court pardoned Xicai.

sentences.zh: 以河南副元帥、黃門侍郎、同平章事王縉為幽州節度使，授希彩御史中丞，充幽州節度副使，權知軍州事，詔縉赴鎮。

translations.literal: Wang Jin, deputy commander-in-chief of Henan, vice director of the Yellow Gate, and fellow chief minister, was made military governor of Youzhou; Xicai was appointed vice censor-in-chief and deputy military governor of Youzhou with provisional authority over army and prefecture affairs, and an edict ordered Jin to proceed to the post.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, deputy commander of Henan, vice director of the Yellow Gate, and fellow chief minister, was made Youzhou governor; Xicai was made vice censor-in-chief and deputy Youzhou governor with provisional control of army and prefecture affairs, and Jin was ordered to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 希彩聞縉之來，搜選卒伍，大陳戎備以逆之。

translations.literal: When Xicai heard Jin was coming, he searched out and selected troops and greatly arrayed military preparations to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Jin's approach, Xicai mustered troops and made elaborate military preparations to resist him.

sentences.zh: 縉晏然建旌節，而希彩迎謁甚恭。

translations.literal: Jin calmly raised his banners and insignia, while Xicai received and paid respects with great deference.
translations.idiomatic: Jin calmly established his banners and insignia; Xicai met him with elaborate deference.

sentences.zh: 縉知終不可制，勞軍旬日而還。

translations.literal: Jin knew he could never control him, reviewed the troops for ten days, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could never control Xicai, Jin reviewed the troops for ten days and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋加希彩御史大夫，充幽州節度留後。

translations.literal: Soon Xicai was further promoted to chief censor and acting military governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xicai was soon promoted to chief censor and acting Youzhou governor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，加希彩幽州大都督府長史、幽州盧龍軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was further made chief administrator of the Youzhou metropolitan prefecture and military governor of the Youzhou Lulong army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was further made chief administrator of Youzhou and military governor of the Youzhou Lulong army.

sentences.zh: 五年，封高密郡王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was enfeoffed Prince of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 既得位，暴橫自恣，無禮於朝廷。

translations.literal: Once he had gained his position, he was violent and willful and showed no deference to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Once established in power, he was violent and unrestrained and showed no deference to court.

sentences.zh: 七年，孔目官李瑗因人之怒，伺隙斬之，軍人立其兵馬使硃泚為留後。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the clerical officer Li Yuan, taking advantage of popular anger, seized an opening and beheaded him; the soldiers installed his army and horse commissioner Zhu Ci as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, the clerical officer Li Yuan, exploiting popular anger, killed him at an opportune moment; the troops installed his army and horse commissioner Zhu Ci as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 泚自有傳。

translations.literal: Ci has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Ci has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 硃滔，賊泚之弟也。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao was the younger brother of the rebel Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao was the younger brother of the rebel Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 平州刺史硃希彩為幽州節度，以滔同姓，甚愛之，常令將腹心親兵。

translations.literal: Zhu Xicai of Ping prefecture was military governor of Youzhou; because Tao was of the same surname, he loved him greatly and often had him lead his trusted personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xicai of Pingzhou was Youzhou governor; as Tao shared his surname, he favored him and often had him lead trusted personal troops.

sentences.zh: 及泚為節度使，遂使滔將勁兵三千赴京師，請率先諸軍備塞。

translations.literal: When Ci became military governor, he sent Tao at the head of three thousand crack troops to the capital to request that he lead the various armies in guarding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci became governor, he sent Tao with three thousand crack troops to the capital to ask to lead the armies in frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 自祿山反後，山東范陽，外雖示順，實皆倔強不庭。

translations.literal: After Lushan's rebellion, east of the mountains in Fanyang, though outwardly they showed submission, in truth all were stubborn and would not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: After Lushan's rebellion, Fanyang east of the mountains outwardly submitted but in truth remained stubbornly insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 泚首效臣節，代宗喜甚，命滔勒兵東入長安通化門，西出開遠門，出師勞還；

translations.literal: Ci was the first to demonstrate ministerial loyalty; Emperor Daizong was greatly pleased and ordered Tao to lead troops east through the Tonghua Gate of Chang'an and west out the Kaiyuan Gate, going out to review the army on its departure and return;
translations.idiomatic: Ci was first to demonstrate loyal service; Daizong was greatly pleased and had Tao lead troops east through Chang'an's Tonghua Gate and west out the Kaiyuan Gate, reviewing the army on departure and return;

sentences.zh: 未有兵還王城者，今而許之，蓋示優異。

translations.literal: never before had troops returning to the royal city been permitted—now it was allowed, plainly to show special favor.
translations.idiomatic: never before had returning troops been allowed into the capital—now permission was granted as a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 召滔對於三殿，代宗臨軒勞問。

translations.literal: Tao was summoned to audience in the Three Halls; Emperor Daizong, seated at the front of the hall, inquired and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was summoned to the Three Halls; Daizong received him from the imperial dais and questioned him with commendation.

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「卿材孰與泚多？」

translations.literal: Then he said, "Between your talent and Ci's, whose is the greater?"
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "Between your talent and Ci's, whose is the greater?"

sentences.zh: 滔曰：「各有長短。

translations.literal: Tao said, "Each has strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Tao said, "Each has strengths and weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 統御士眾，方略明辨，臣不及泚；

translations.literal: In commanding troops and setting strategy with clear discrimination, I do not match Ci;
translations.idiomatic: In commanding troops and discerning strategy, I do not match Ci;

sentences.zh: 臣年二十八，獲謁龍顏，泚長臣五歲，未朝鳳闕，此不及臣。」

translations.literal: I am twenty-eight and have been granted audience with the imperial countenance; Ci is five years my elder and has not attended court at Fengque—there I do not match him."
translations.idiomatic: I am twenty-eight and have been granted audience with the throne; Ci is five years older and has never attended court at Fengque—in that I surpass him."

sentences.zh: 代宗愈喜。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong was all the more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong was all the more pleased.

sentences.zh: 泚既僭號，立滔為皇太弟，仍令以重賂招誘回紇，南攻魏、貝，即西入關。

translations.literal: When Ci usurped the throne, he installed Tao as imperial younger brother and also ordered him to use heavy bribes to entice the Huige, attack Wei and Bei in the south, and then enter the passes westward.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci usurped the throne, he made Tao imperial younger brother and ordered him to use heavy bribes to win over the Huige, attack Wei and Bei in the south, and then advance west through the passes.

sentences.zh: 興元元年正月，滔驅率燕、薊之眾及回紇雜虜，號五萬，次南河，攻圍貝州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xingyuan, Tao drove the masses of Yan and Ji and mixed Huige and other barbarians, numbering fifty thousand, to camp south of the river and besiege Bei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xingyuan 1, Tao drove Yan and Ji forces and mixed Huige and other tribes, fifty thousand strong, to camp south of the river and besiege Bei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，田緒殺田悅，魏州亂。

translations.literal: In the third month, Tian Xu killed Tian Yue and Wei prefecture fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Tian Xu killed Tian Yue and Wei prefecture was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 滔令大將馬實分兵逼魏州，營於王莽河。

translations.literal: Tao ordered his great general Ma Shi to divide troops and press Wei prefecture, encamping at the Manghe River.
translations.idiomatic: Tao ordered his general Ma Shi to split forces and press Wei prefecture, encamping at the Manghe River.

sentences.zh: 德宗在山南，慮二兇兵合，遣使授王武俊平章事，令與李抱真葉力擊滔。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong was in the southern mountains and, fearing the two rebels' armies would unite, sent envoys to appoint Wang Wujun chief minister and order him to join Li Baozhen in striking Tao with combined force.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong, in the southern mountains, feared the two rebel armies would unite and sent envoys to appoint Wang Wujun chief minister and order him to join Li Baozhen in attacking Tao.

sentences.zh: 四月，恆、潞兩軍次涇城北，行營相距十里；

translations.literal: In the fourth month the Heng and Lu armies halted north of Jing city, their camps ten li apart;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Heng and Lu armies halted north of Jing city, their camps ten li apart;

sentences.zh: 抱真自率二百騎徑入武俊軍，面申盟約，結為兄弟。

translations.literal: Baozhen personally led two hundred horsemen straight into Wujun's camp, stated the covenant face to face, and became sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen personally led two hundred horsemen directly into Wujun's camp, affirmed their alliance face to face, and became sworn brothers.

sentences.zh: 五月四日，進軍距貝州三十里而軍。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the fifth month they advanced and encamped thirty li from Bei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth month's fourth day they advanced and encamped thirty li from Bei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 翌日，滔令大將馬實、盧南史引回紇、契丹來挑戰，武俊遣騎將趙珍提精騎三百當之，抱真將王虔休掎角待之。

translations.literal: The next day Tao ordered his great generals Ma Shi and Lu Nanshi to lead Huige and Khitan forces to challenge battle; Wujun sent his cavalry commander Zhao Zhen with three hundred picked horsemen to meet them, and Baozhen's officer Wang Qianxiu waited at an angle to support him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Tao ordered Ma Shi and Lu Nanshi to lead Huige and Khitan forces into battle; Wujun sent Zhao Zhen with three hundred picked horsemen to meet them, while Baozhen's Wang Qianxiu waited to strike from the flank.

sentences.zh: 武俊與其子士清自當回紇、契丹部落。

translations.literal: Wujun and his son Shiqing personally faced the Huige and Khitan tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun and his son Shiqing personally faced the Huige and Khitan tribes.

sentences.zh: 兩軍既合，鼓噪震地，回紇恃捷，穿武俊陣而過。

translations.literal: Once the two armies joined, the clamor of drums and shouts shook the earth; relying on recent victories, the Huige pierced through Wujun's formation.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies clashed, drum and shout shook the earth; trusting recent victories, the Huige drove through Wujun's line.

sentences.zh: 武俊乘騎勒馬不動，俟回紇引退，因而薄之，回紇勢不能止。

translations.literal: Wujun sat his horse and held still; when the Huige drew back he pressed them, and the Huige could not check their momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun held his horse motionless; as the Huige withdrew he pressed them, and they could not stop their momentum.

sentences.zh: 武俊父子縱馬急擊，獲回紇三百騎。

translations.literal: Wujun and his son spurred their horses in fierce attack and captured three hundred Huige horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son spurred their horses in fierce attack and captured three hundred Huige horsemen.

sentences.zh: 滔陣亂，東走，兩邊追斬，俘馘數萬計。

translations.literal: Tao's formation broke and he fled east; pursuers on both sides cut down and captured tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's line broke and he fled east; pursuers on both flanks cut down and captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 遇夜，夾滔壘而軍。

translations.literal: When night fell they encamped on both sides of Tao's ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: At nightfall they encamped on both sides of Tao's fortifications.

sentences.zh: 是夜，滔以殘眾千人奔德州，委棄戈甲山積。

translations.literal: That night Tao fled to De prefecture with a remnant of a thousand men, abandoning weapons and armor heaped like hills.
translations.idiomatic: That night Tao fled to Dezhou with a thousand survivors, abandoning weapons and armor heaped like hills.

sentences.zh: 滔至瀛州，殺騎將蔡雄、揚布。

translations.literal: When Tao reached Ying prefecture he killed the cavalry commanders Cai Xiong and Yang Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Yingzhou, Tao killed his cavalry commanders Cai Xiong and Yang Bu.

sentences.zh: 以其前鋒先敗，又殺陰陽人尹少伯，以其言舉兵必勝故也。

translations.literal: Because the vanguard had been defeated first, he also killed the yin-yang master Yin Shaobo, since it was on his word that raising troops would surely bring victory.
translations.idiomatic: Because the vanguard had failed first, he also killed the yin-yang master Yin Shaobo, who had declared that raising troops would surely bring victory.

sentences.zh: 六月，李晟收京城，硃泚、姚令言死。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Li Sheng recovered the capital; Zhu Ci and Yao Lingyan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Li Sheng recovered the capital; Zhu Ci and Yao Lingyan died.

sentences.zh: 滔還幽州，為武俊所攻，僅不能軍，上章待罪。

translations.literal: Tao returned to Youzhou, was attacked by Wujun, and barely kept his army intact; he submitted a memorial awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Tao returned to Youzhou, was attacked by Wujun, and barely held his army together; he submitted a memorial awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔曰：「硃滔累獻款疏，深效懇誠，省之惻然，良用憫嘆！

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict said, "Zhu Tao has repeatedly submitted letters of submission and shown deep sincerity; reading them moves one to compassion, and one cannot help sighing in pity!
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict said, "Zhu Tao has repeatedly submitted letters of submission and shown deep sincerity; reading them moves one to compassion, and one cannot help sighing in pity!

sentences.zh: 宜委武俊、抱真開示大信，深加曉諭。

translations.literal: Wujun and Baozhen should be entrusted to declare great faith and instruct him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun and Baozhen should be entrusted to declare great faith and instruct him deeply.

sentences.zh: 若誠心益固，善跡克彰，朕當掩釁錄勛，與之昭雪。」

translations.literal: If his sincere heart grows firmer and good conduct is fully displayed, We shall cover past offenses and record merit, clearing him of blame."
translations.idiomatic: If his sincere heart grows firmer and good conduct is fully displayed, We shall cover past offenses and record merit, clearing him of blame."

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，尋卒於位，時年四十，贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan he soon died in office at the age of forty and was posthumously made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 he soon died in office at forty and was posthumously made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 劉怦，幽州昌平人也。

translations.literal: Liu Peng was a man of Changping in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Peng was from Changping in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 父貢，嘗為廣邊大鬥軍使。

translations.literal: His father Gong had once been commissioner of the Guangbian Great Garrison Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gong had served as commissioner of the Guangbian Great Garrison Army.

sentences.zh: 怦即硃滔姑之子，積軍功為雄武軍使，廣屯田，節用，以辦理稱。

translations.literal: Peng was the son of Zhu Tao's sister; through accumulated military merit he became commissioner of the Xiongwu Army, broadly managed garrison agriculture, practiced economy, and was known for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: Peng was Zhu Tao's nephew by marriage; through accumulated military merit he became commissioner of the Xiongwu Army, managed garrison agriculture broadly, practiced economy, and was known for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 稍遷涿州刺史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to governor of Zhuo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to governor of Zhuo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 居數年，硃滔將兵討田承嗣，奏署怦領留府事，以寬緩得眾心。

translations.literal: After several years, when Zhu Tao led troops to attack Tian Chengsi, he memorialized to appoint Peng to manage affairs in the provisional headquarters; through lenient and steady rule he won the hearts of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: After several years, when Zhu Tao led troops against Tian Chengsi, he appointed Peng to manage the provisional headquarters; through lenient rule he won popular support.

sentences.zh: 時李寶臣為田承嗣間說，與之通謀。

translations.literal: At that time Li Baochen, persuaded by Tian Chengsi, joined in a secret plot with him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Baochen, persuaded by Tian Chengsi, entered into secret collusion with him.

sentences.zh: 承嗣又以滄州與寶臣，乃以兵劫硃滔於瓦橋關，滔脫身走，乘勝欲襲取幽州。

translations.literal: Chengshi also gave Cang prefecture to Baochen; he then sent troops to seize Zhu Tao at Waqiao Pass—Tao escaped, and pursuing victory he wished to strike and take Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi also ceded Cangzhou to Baochen, who then sent troops to seize Zhu Tao at Waqiao Pass; Tao escaped, and Baochen pressed his advantage to strike at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 怦設方略鎮撫，寶臣不敢進，以功加御史中丞。

translations.literal: Peng devised strategy to pacify and reassure; Baochen did not dare advance, and for this service Peng was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Peng devised strategy to pacify the situation; Baochen did not dare advance, and Peng was promoted to vice censor-in-chief for this service.

sentences.zh: 寶臣死，子惟嶽拒朝命，德宗令滔與張孝忠同力討之。

translations.literal: When Baochen died, his son Weiyue defied the court's orders; Emperor Dezong ordered Tao and Zhang Xiaozhong to join forces in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: When Baochen died, his son Weiyue defied court orders; Dezong ordered Tao and Zhang Xiaozhong to attack him jointly.

sentences.zh: 及惟嶽平，滔怨朝廷違約不與深州，含怒不已。

translations.literal: When Weiyue was pacified, Tao resented the court for breaking its promise and not granting Shen prefecture, and nursed anger without end.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiyue was pacified, Tao resented the court for breaking its promise to grant Shenzhou and nursed unending anger.

sentences.zh: 會王武俊亦怨割地深、趙，相謀叛，欲救田悅。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun also resented the cession of Shen and Zhao prefectures and plotted rebellion together, intending to rescue Tian Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun also resented losing Shen and Zhao prefectures and joined the plot to rebel and rescue Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 怦時知幽州留後事，遣人賫書謂滔曰：「司徒位崇太尉，尊居宰相，恩寵冠籓臣之右，榮遇極矣！

translations.literal: Peng was then managing provisional affairs at Youzhou and sent someone bearing a letter saying to Tao, "Your Excellency's rank is exalted as Grand Marshal and your honor stands as chief minister; imperial favor crowns all frontier ministers—your glory has reached its height!
translations.idiomatic: Peng was then managing provisional affairs at Youzhou and sent a letter saying to Tao, "Your Excellency's rank is exalted as Grand Marshal and your honor stands as chief minister; imperial favor crowns all frontier ministers—your glory has reached its height!

sentences.zh: 今昌平故裏，朝廷改為尉卿、司徒裏，此亦大夫不朽之名也。

translations.literal: Your old home at Changping—the court has renamed it Weiqing and Situli Lane—this too is an immortal name for a great officer.
translations.idiomatic: Your old home at Changping—the court has renamed it Weiqing and Situli Lane—this too is an immortal name for a great officer.

sentences.zh: 但以忠順自持，則事無不濟。

translations.literal: If you hold to loyalty and submission, nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: If you hold to loyalty and submission, nothing will fail.

sentences.zh: 竊思近日，務大樂戰，不顧成敗，而家滅身屠者，安、史是也。

translations.literal: I privately reflect that in recent days those who devoted themselves to great battles, heedless of success or failure, and saw their families destroyed and themselves slaughtered—An and Shi were such men.
translations.idiomatic: I privately reflect that in recent days those who devoted themselves to great battles, heedless of success or failure, and saw their families destroyed and themselves slaughtered—An and Shi were such men.

sentences.zh: 暴亂易亡，今復何有？

translations.literal: Violent rebellion is easily destroyed—what of it now?
translations.idiomatic: Violent rebellion is easily destroyed—what of it now?

sentences.zh: 怦忝密親，世荷恩遇，默而無告，是負重知。

translations.literal: Peng, though unworthy, is your close kinsman and has received imperial grace through generations; to keep silent and not inform you would betray deep trust.
translations.idiomatic: Peng, though unworthy, is your close kinsman and has received imperial grace through generations; to keep silent and not inform you would betray deep trust.

sentences.zh: 惟司徒圖之，無貽後悔也！」

translations.literal: I only ask Your Excellency to consider this and leave no cause for regret!"
translations.idiomatic: I only ask Your Excellency to consider this and leave no cause for regret!"

sentences.zh: 滔雖不用其言，亦嘉其盡言，卒無疑貳。

translations.literal: Although Tao did not heed his words, he also commended his frank counsel and in the end harbored no suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Although Tao did not heed his words, he commended his frank counsel and in the end harbored no suspicion.

sentences.zh: 凡出征伐，必以怦總留後事。

translations.literal: Whenever he marched on campaign he always had Peng manage provisional affairs in his absence.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he marched on campaign he always left Peng to manage provisional affairs.

sentences.zh: 及僭稱大冀王，偽署怦為右僕射、范陽留守。

translations.literal: When he falsely styled himself King of Great Ji, he falsely appointed Peng right vice minister and acting garrison commander of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When he falsely styled himself King of Great Ji, he falsely appointed Peng right vice minister and acting garrison commander of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 及泚據京邑，召滔南河，至貝州，挫敗而還，兵甲盡喪。

translations.literal: When Ci held the capital, he summoned Tao south of the river; Tao reached Bei prefecture, was defeated and driven back, and lost all arms and armor.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci held the capital, he summoned Tao south of the river; Tao reached Bei prefecture, was defeated and driven back, and lost all arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 怦聞滔將至，悉蒐范陽兵甲，夾道排列二十餘里，以迎滔歸於府第，人皆嘉怦忠義。

translations.literal: When Peng heard Tao was about to arrive, he gathered all Fanyang arms and armor and lined both sides of the road for more than twenty li to welcome Tao back to his residence; all praised Peng's loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng heard Tao was returning, he gathered all Fanyang arms and armor and lined both sides of the road for more than twenty li to welcome Tao home; all praised his loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，滔卒，三軍推怦權撫軍府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan Tao died; the three armies pushed Peng to manage the military headquarters provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 Tao died; the three armies pushed Peng to manage the headquarters provisionally.

sentences.zh: 怦為眾所服，卒有其地。

translations.literal: Peng was accepted by the masses and in the end held the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Accepted by the troops, Peng in the end held the territory.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因授怦幽州大都督府長史、兼御史大夫、幽州盧龍節度副大使、知節度事、管內營田觀察、押奚契丹、經略盧龍軍使。

translations.literal: The court thereupon appointed Peng chief administrator of the Youzhou metropolitan prefecture, concurrent chief censor, deputy military governor of Youzhou and Lulong, with control of military affairs, supervision of garrison agriculture within the circuit, oversight of the Xi and Khitan, and commissioner of the Lulong army.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Peng chief administrator of Youzhou, concurrent chief censor, deputy Youzhou and Lulong governor with control of military affairs, supervision of garrison agriculture, oversight of the Xi and Khitan, and commissioner of the Lulong army.

sentences.zh: 居位三月，以貞元元年九月卒，年五十九，廢朝三日，贈兵部尚書，賜布帛有差。

translations.literal: After three months in office, in the ninth month of the first year of Zhenyuan he died at fifty-nine; court was suspended for three days, he was posthumously made minister of war, and silks were granted in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: After three months in office, in the ninth month of Zhenyuan 1 he died at fifty-nine; court was suspended three days, he was posthumously made minister of war, and silks were granted in due measure.

sentences.zh: 子濟繼為幽州節度使。

translations.literal: His son Ji succeeded him as military governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji succeeded him as Youzhou governor.

sentences.zh: 濟，怦之長子。

translations.literal: Ji was Peng's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was Peng's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 初，母難產；

translations.literal: At first his mother had a difficult labor;
translations.idiomatic: At first his mother had a difficult labor;

sentences.zh: 既產，侍者初見濟是一大蛇，黑氣勃勃，莫不驚走。

translations.literal: once he was born, the attendants at first sight saw Ji as a great serpent; black vapor swelled forth and all fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: once born, attendants at first sight saw Ji as a great serpent; black vapor swelled forth and all fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗異常童。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was quite unlike an ordinary child.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he was quite unlike an ordinary child.

sentences.zh: 所居室焚，人皆驚救，濟從容而出，眾異之。

translations.literal: The dwelling where he lived burned; all were alarmed and rushed to rescue him, but Ji walked out at ease and the crowd marveled.
translations.idiomatic: The dwelling where he lived burned; all rushed to rescue him, but Ji walked out at ease and the crowd marveled.

sentences.zh: 累歷本管州縣牧宰。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of prefect and magistrate within the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He successively held prefectural and magisterial posts within the circuit.

sentences.zh: 及怦為節度使，以濟兼御史中丞，充行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Peng became military governor, Ji was made vice censor-in-chief and acting army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng became governor, Ji was made vice censor-in-chief and acting army marshal.

sentences.zh: 怦卒，軍人習河朔舊事，請濟代父為帥，朝廷姑務便安，因而從之。

translations.literal: When Peng died, the soldiers, accustomed to old Hebei practice, asked Ji to replace his father as commander; the court for the moment pursued convenience and assent, and so followed their wish.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng died, the soldiers, accustomed to Hebei custom, asked Ji to replace his father; the court pursued convenience and assented.

sentences.zh: 累加至檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to acting minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to acting minister of war.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，遷左僕射，充幽州節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan he was transferred to left vice minister and made military governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 5 he was transferred to left vice minister and made Youzhou governor.

sentences.zh: 時烏桓、鮮卑數寇邊，濟率軍擊走之；

translations.literal: At that time the Wuhuan and Xianbei repeatedly raided the frontier; Ji led troops in attack and drove them off;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Wuhuan and Xianbei repeatedly raided the frontier; Ji led troops and drove them off;

sentences.zh: 深入千餘里，虜獲不可勝紀，東北晏然。

translations.literal: penetrating more than a thousand li, captives and booty were beyond counting, and the northeast was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: penetrating more than a thousand li, captives and booty were beyond counting, and the northeast was tranquil.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，朝廷優容籓鎮方甚，兩河擅自繼襲者，尤驕蹇不奉法。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era the court greatly indulged frontier commands, and those in the two He provinces who on their own succeeded by inheritance were especially arrogant and would not obey law.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era the court greatly indulged frontier commands, and those in the two He provinces who succeeded by inheritance were especially arrogant and lawless.

sentences.zh: 惟濟最務恭順，朝獻相繼，德宗亦以恩禮接之。

translations.literal: Only Ji most diligently pursued respectful submission; tribute missions followed one after another, and Emperor Dezong also received him with favor and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ji most diligently pursued respectful submission; tribute missions followed in succession, and Dezong received him with favor and ritual.

sentences.zh: 尋加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was soon further made fellow chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further made fellow chief minister.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，再遷檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong acceded, he was again promoted to acting chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong acceded, he was again promoted to acting chief minister.

sentences.zh: 元和初，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was further made concurrent chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was further made concurrent chief minister.

sentences.zh: 及詔討王承宗，諸軍未進，濟獨率先前軍擊破之，生擒三百余人，斬首千余級，獻逆將於闕，優詔褒之。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered the campaign against Wang Chengzong and the various armies had not yet advanced, Ji alone led the vanguard first, broke the enemy, captured more than three hundred alive, and beheaded more than a thousand; he presented the rebel generals at court and received an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the campaign against Wang Chengzong and the armies had not advanced, Ji alone led the vanguard, broke the enemy, captured more than three hundred alive and beheaded more than a thousand; he presented rebel generals at court and received praise.

sentences.zh: 又為詩四韻上獻，以表忠憤之誌。

translations.literal: He also composed a four-line poem and presented it upward, to express the will of loyal indignation.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed a four-line poem and presented it upward to express loyal indignation.

sentences.zh: 明年春，將大軍次瀛州，累攻樂壽、博陸、安平等縣，前後大獻俘獲。

translations.literal: The next spring he led a great army to halt at Ying prefecture and repeatedly attacked Lexian, Bolu, and Ping'an counties; before and after he greatly presented captives.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he led a great army to Yingzhou and repeatedly attacked Lexian, Bolu, and Ping'an counties, presenting many captives.

sentences.zh: 賞功頗厚，仍與子孫六品官者凡四人。

translations.literal: Rewards for merit were quite generous; six persons among his sons and grandsons received sixth-rank offices.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards for merit were generous; six of his sons and grandsons received sixth-rank offices.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有疾，會赦承宗，錄功拜兼中書令。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill; when an amnesty restored Chengzong, his merit was recorded and he was appointed concurrent chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill; when an amnesty restored Chengzong, his merit was recorded and he was appointed concurrent chief minister.

sentences.zh: 濟在鎮二十余年，雖輸忠款，竟不入覲。

translations.literal: Ji held the post more than twenty years; though he offered loyal submission, in the end he never entered court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Ji held the post more than twenty years; though he offered loyal submission, he never attended court.

sentences.zh: 又謀殺其弟澭，澭歸國為信臣。

translations.literal: He also plotted to kill his younger brother Yong; Yong returned to the empire and became a trusted minister.
translations.idiomatic: He also plotted to kill his younger brother Yong; Yong returned to the empire and became a trusted minister.

sentences.zh: 及濟疾，次子總與濟親吏唐弘實通謀鴆殺濟，數日，乃發喪。

translations.literal: When Ji fell ill, his second son Zong joined with Ji's personal clerk Tang Hongshi in a plot to poison and kill Ji; only after several days did they announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji fell ill, his second son Zong joined Ji's personal clerk Tang Hongshi in poisoning him; only after several days did they announce mourning.

sentences.zh: 時年五十四，詔贈太師，廢朝三日，賻禮有加，謚曰莊武。

translations.literal: He was fifty-four; an edict posthumously made him grand preceptor, court was suspended three days, funeral gifts were increased, and his posthumous title was Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-four; an edict posthumously made him grand preceptor, court was suspended three days, funeral gifts were increased, and his posthumous title was Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 弟源，貞元十六年八月，為檢校工部尚書，兼左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yuan, in the eighth month of the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan, was made acting minister of works and concurrent left Wuwei general.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuan, in the eighth month of Zhenyuan 16, was made acting minister of works and concurrent left Wuwei general.

sentences.zh: 初，為涿州刺史，不受兄教令，濟奏之，貶漠州參軍，復不受詔。

translations.literal: At first he was governor of Zhuo prefecture and would not accept his elder brother's orders; Ji memorialized against him and he was demoted to army adjutant of Mo prefecture, but again would not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was governor of Zhuo prefecture and refused his elder brother's orders; Ji memorialized against him and he was demoted to Mo prefecture army adjutant, but again refused the edict.

sentences.zh: 濟帥師至涿州，源出兵拒之，未合而自潰。

translations.literal: Ji led troops to Zhuo prefecture; Yuan led troops out to resist him, and before joining battle his force dissolved on its own.
translations.idiomatic: Ji led troops to Zhuo prefecture; Yuan led troops out to resist, and before battle his force dissolved.

sentences.zh: 濟擒源至幽州，上言請令入覲，故授官以征之。

translations.literal: Ji captured Yuan and brought him to Youzhou; he submitted a memorial asking that Yuan be ordered to attend court, and so an office was granted to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji captured Yuan and brought him to Youzhou; he submitted a memorial asking that Yuan attend court, and an office was granted to summon him.

sentences.zh: 澭，濟之異母弟也。

translations.literal: Yong was Ji's younger brother by a different mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was Ji's younger brother by a different mother.

sentences.zh: 喜讀書，工武藝，輕財愛士，得人死力。

translations.literal: He loved reading books, was skilled in martial arts, was generous with wealth and cherished officers, and won men's strength unto death.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading, was skilled in martial arts, generous with wealth and cherished officers, and won men's strength unto death.

sentences.zh: 事硃滔，常陳逆順之理。

translations.literal: Serving Zhu Tao, he often set forth the principle of loyalty and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Zhu Tao, he often set forth the principle of loyalty versus rebellion.

sentences.zh: 後怦為盧龍軍節度使，病將卒，澭在父側，即以父命召兄濟自漠州至，竟得授節度使。

translations.literal: Later, when Peng became military governor of the Lulong army and was ill and about to die, Yong was at his father's side and immediately on his father's order summoned his elder brother Ji from Mo prefecture; in the end Ji received appointment as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Peng was Lulong governor and lay ill near death, Yong was at his side and on his father's order summoned Ji from Mo prefecture; Ji in the end received the governorship.

sentences.zh: 濟常感澭奉己，

translations.literal: Ji always felt gratitude that Yong had supported him,
translations.idiomatic: Ji always felt gratitude that Yong had supported him,

sentences.zh: 澭為瀛州刺史，亦許以澭代己任；

translations.literal: Yong was governor of Ying prefecture, and Ji also promised that Yong would replace him in office;
translations.idiomatic: Yong was governor of Ying prefecture, and Ji also promised Yong would replace him;

sentences.zh: 其後濟乃以其子為副大使。

translations.literal: afterward Ji made his own son deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: afterward Ji made his own son deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 澭既怒濟，遂請以所部西捍隴塞，拔其所部兵一千五百人、男女萬余口直趨京師，在道無一人犯令者。

translations.literal: Yong, angered at Ji, then asked to lead his command west to defend the Long frontier, mustered fifteen hundred troops and more than ten thousand men and women of his command, and marched straight for the capital; on the road not a single person violated orders.
translations.idiomatic: Angered at Ji, Yong asked to lead his command west to defend the Long frontier, mustered fifteen hundred troops and more than ten thousand men and women, and marched straight for the capital; on the road not one person violated orders.

sentences.zh: 德宗寵遇，特授秦州刺史，以普潤縣為理所。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong favored and received him and specially appointed him governor of Qin prefecture, making Pu-run county his seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong favored him and specially appointed him governor of Qin prefecture, with Pu-run county as his seat.

sentences.zh: 及順宗傳位，稱太上皇，有山人羅令則詣澭言異端數百言，皆廢立之事，澭立命系之。

translations.literal: When Shunzong transmitted the throne and styled himself retired emperor, the mountain man Luo Lingze came to Yong and spoke several hundred words of heterodox doctrine, all concerning deposition and installation; Yong immediately ordered him bound.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong abdicated and styled himself retired emperor, the mountain man Luo Lingze came to Yong with several hundred words of heterodox doctrine on deposition and installation; Yong immediately ordered him bound.

sentences.zh: 令則又雲某之黨多矣，約以德宗山陵時伺便而動。

translations.literal: Lingze also said that his faction was many and that they planned to act when convenient at the time of Dezong's tomb mounting.
translations.idiomatic: Lingze also said his faction was numerous and planned to act when convenient at Dezong's tomb mounting.

sentences.zh: 澭械令則送京師，杖死之。

translations.literal: Yong shackled Lingze and sent him to the capital, where he was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yong shackled Lingze and sent him to the capital, where he was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 後錄功，賜其額曰保義。

translations.literal: Later his merit was recorded and his district was granted the title Baoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Later his merit was recorded and his district was granted the title Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 其軍蕃戎畏之，不敢為寇，常有復河湟之誌，議者壯之。

translations.literal: His army was feared by the frontier tribes, who did not dare raid; he often had the will to recover the He and Huang regions, and commentators admired him.
translations.idiomatic: His army was feared by frontier tribes, who did not dare raid; he often aspired to recover the He and Huang regions, and commentators admired him.

sentences.zh: 元和二年十二月，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanhe he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Yuanhe 2 he died.

sentences.zh: 總，濟之第二子也，性陰賊險譎。

translations.literal: Zong was Ji's second son; by nature he was secretive, vicious, and treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was Ji's second son; by nature he was secretive, vicious, and treacherous.

sentences.zh: 元和五年，濟奉詔討王承宗，使長子緄假為副使，領留務。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanhe, when Ji received an edict to campaign against Wang Chengzong, he sent his eldest son Wan to serve falsely as deputy commissioner and manage provisional affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 5, when Ji received an edict to campaign against Wang Chengzong, he sent his eldest son Wan falsely as deputy commissioner to manage provisional affairs.

sentences.zh: 時總為瀛州刺史，濟署為行營都兵馬使，屯軍饒陽，師久無功。

translations.literal: At that time Zong was governor of Ying prefecture; Ji appointed him camp commander of all army and horse forces, encamping at Raoyang; the campaign was long without success.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zong was governor of Ying prefecture; Ji appointed him camp commander of all forces, encamping at Raoyang; the campaign dragged on without success.

sentences.zh: 總潛伺其隙，與判官張、孔目官成國寶及帳內小將為謀，使詐自京至，曰：「朝廷以相公逗留不進，除副大使為節度使矣。」

translations.literal: Zong secretly watched for an opening and, with the judicial officer Zhang, the clerical officer Cheng Guobao, and junior officers of the inner guard, plotted; he had someone falsely arrive from the capital, saying, "The court, because the Chancellor delayed and did not advance, has appointed the deputy commissioner military governor."
translations.idiomatic: Zong secretly watched for an opening and, with judicial officer Zhang, clerical officer Cheng Guobao, and inner-guard junior officers, plotted; he had someone falsely arrive from the capital, saying, "The court, because the Chancellor delayed and did not advance, has appointed the deputy commissioner military governor."

sentences.zh: 明日，又使人曰：「副大使旌節已到太原。」

translations.literal: The next day he again sent someone saying, "The deputy commissioner's banners and insignia have reached Taiyuan."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he again sent someone saying, "The deputy commissioner's banners and insignia have reached Taiyuan."

sentences.zh: 又使人走而呼曰：「旌節過代州。」

translations.literal: Again he sent someone running to shout, "The banners and insignia have passed Daizhou."
translations.idiomatic: Again he sent someone running to shout, "The banners and insignia have passed Daizhou."

sentences.zh: 舉軍驚恐。

translations.literal: The entire army was alarmed and terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The entire army was alarmed and terrified.

sentences.zh: 濟驚惶憤怒，不知所為，因殺主兵大將數十人及與緄素厚者。

translations.literal: Ji was alarmed, angry, and at a loss; he therefore killed several dozen chief generals and those close to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was alarmed, angry, and at a loss; he killed several dozen chief generals and those close to Wan.

sentences.zh: 乃追緄，以張兄臯代知留務。

translations.literal: He then recalled Wan and had Zhang's elder brother Gao replace him in managing provisional affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then recalled Wan and had Zhang's elder brother Gao replace him in managing provisional affairs.

sentences.zh: 濟自朝至日晏不食，渴索飲，總因置毒而進之。

translations.literal: From morning until evening Ji ate nothing; parched with thirst he asked for drink, and Zong placed poison in it and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: From morning until evening Ji ate nothing; parched with thirst he asked for drink, and Zong placed poison in it and presented it.

sentences.zh: 濟死，緄行至涿州，總矯以父命杖殺之，總遂領軍務。

translations.literal: When Ji died, Wan had reached Zhuo prefecture; Zong forged his father's order and had Wan beaten to death with the staff, and Zong then took command of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji died, Wan had reached Zhuo prefecture; Zong forged his father's order and had Wan beaten to death, and Zong then took command.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不知其事，因授以斧鉞，累遷至檢校司空。

translations.literal: The court did not know of this matter and therefore granted him the axe and halberd of command; he was successively promoted to acting chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not know and granted him command authority; he was successively promoted to acting chief minister.

sentences.zh: 及王承宗再拒命，總遣兵取賊武強縣，遂駐軍持兩端，以利朝廷供饋賞賜。

translations.literal: When Wang Chengzong again defied orders, Zong sent troops to take the rebel county Wuqiang and then encamped holding both sides, to profit from court supplies and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong again defied orders, Zong sent troops to take Wuqiang and encamped holding both sides to profit from court supplies and rewards.

sentences.zh: 是時吳元濟尚存，王承宗方跋扈，易定孤危，憲宗暫務姑息，加總同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Yuanji still survived and Wang Chengzong was overbearing; Yiding was isolated and endangered; Emperor Xianzong for the moment pursued indulgence and made Zong fellow chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Yuanji still lived and Wang Chengzong was overbearing; Yiding was isolated; Xianzong for the moment pursued indulgence and made Zong fellow chief minister.

sentences.zh: 及元濟就擒，李師道梟首，王承宗憂死，田弘正入鎮州，總既無黨援，懷懼，每謀自安之計。

translations.literal: When Yuanji was captured, Li Shidao was beheaded, Wang Chengzong died in worry, and Tian Hongzheng entered Zhen prefecture; Zong had no factional support, was fearful, and daily plotted means of self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanji was captured, Li Shidao was beheaded, Wang Chengzong died in worry, and Tian Hongzheng entered Zhenzhou; Zong had no allies, was fearful, and daily plotted self-preservation.

sentences.zh: 初，總弒逆後，每見父兄為祟，甚慘懼，乃於官署後置數百僧，厚給衣食，令晝夜乞恩謝罪。

translations.literal: At first, after Zong's regicide, whenever he saw his father and elder brother as apparitions he was deeply terrified; he therefore placed several hundred monks behind the official quarters, richly supplied with food and clothing, and ordered them day and night to beg grace and confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: After his regicide, whenever Zong saw apparitions of his father and elder brother he was terrified; he placed several hundred monks behind the official quarters, richly supplied, and ordered them day and night to beg grace and confess guilt.

sentences.zh: 每公退，則憩於道場，若入他室，則恟惕不敢寐。

translations.literal: Whenever he left public business he rested in the dharma hall; if he entered another room he was anxious and dared not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he left public business he rested in the dharma hall; in any other room he was anxious and dared not sleep.

sentences.zh: 晚年恐悸尤甚，故請落發為僧，冀以脫禍，乃以判官張臯為留後。

translations.literal: In his later years fear and dread were especially severe; he therefore asked to shave his head and become a monk, hoping to escape calamity, and made the judicial officer Zhang Gao acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years fear was especially severe; he asked to shave his head and become a monk, hoping to escape calamity, and made judicial officer Zhang Gao acting governor.

sentences.zh: 總以落發，上表歸朝，穆宗授天平軍節度使；

translations.literal: When Zong had shaved his head he submitted a memorial returning to court; Emperor Muzong appointed him military governor of the Tianping army;
translations.idiomatic: When Zong had shaved his head he submitted a memorial returning to court; Muzong appointed him Tianping governor;

sentences.zh: 既聞落發，乃賜紫，號大覺師。

translations.literal: when it was learned he had shaved his head, he was granted purple robes and styled Great Awakened Master.
translations.idiomatic: when it was learned he had shaved his head, he was granted purple robes and styled Great Awakened Master.

sentences.zh: 總行至易州界，暴卒。

translations.literal: When Zong reached the border of Yi prefecture he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong reached the border of Yizhou he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 輟朝五日，贈太尉，擇日備禮冊命，賻絹布一千五百段、米粟五百石。

translations.literal: Court was suspended five days; he was posthumously made chief minister; on a chosen day full rites of appointment were performed; funeral gifts were fifteen hundred bolts of silk and five hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended five days; he was posthumously made chief minister; full rites of appointment were performed; funeral gifts were fifteen hundred bolts of silk and five hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 先是，元和初，王承宗阻兵，總父濟備陳征伐之術，請身先之。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the beginning of Yuanhe, when Wang Chengzong obstructed the army, Zong's father Ji fully set forth methods of campaigning and asked to lead in person.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the beginning of Yuanhe, when Wang Chengzong obstructed the army, Ji's father fully set forth campaign methods and asked to lead in person.

sentences.zh: 及出軍，累拔城邑，旋屬被病，不克成功。

translations.literal: When the army went out it successively captured cities and towns; soon afterward he fell ill and could not complete the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When the army went out it successively captured cities; soon afterward he fell ill and could not complete the achievement.

sentences.zh: 總既繼父，願述先誌，且欲盡更河朔舊風。

translations.literal: When Zong succeeded his father he wished to carry out his father's will and also wished fully to change old Hebei customs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong succeeded his father he wished to carry out his father's will and fully change old Hebei customs.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，累疏求入覲，兼請分割所理之地，然後歸朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing he repeatedly submitted memorials asking to attend court and also asking to divide the territory he governed and then return to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Changqing he repeatedly submitted memorials asking to attend court and to divide his territory before returning.

sentences.zh: 其意欲以幽、涿、營州為一道，請弘靖理之；

translations.literal: His intent was to make You, Zhuo, and Ying prefectures one circuit and ask Hongjing to govern it;
translations.idiomatic: His intent was to make You, Zhuo, and Ying prefectures one circuit under Hongjing;

sentences.zh: 瀛州、漠州為一道，請盧士玫理之；

translations.literal: Ying and Mo prefectures one circuit and ask Lu Shimei to govern it;
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Mo prefectures one circuit under Lu Shimei;

sentences.zh: 平、薊、媯、檀為一道，請薛平理之。

translations.literal: Ping, Ji, Gui, and Tan one circuit and ask Xue Ping to govern it.
translations.idiomatic: Ping, Ji, Gui, and Tan one circuit under Xue Ping.

sentences.zh: 仍籍軍中宿將盡薦於闕下，因望朝廷升獎，使幽薊之人皆有希羨爵祿之意。

translations.literal: He still registered all veteran generals of the army and recommended them all at court, thereby hoping the court would promote and reward them and make the people of You and Ji all aspire to rank and stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He still registered all veteran generals and recommended them at court, hoping promotion and reward would make the people of You and Ji aspire to rank and stipend.

sentences.zh: 及疏上，穆宗且欲速得范陽，宰臣崔植、杜元穎又不為久大經略，但欲重弘靖所授，而未能省其使局，惟瀛、漠兩州許置觀察使，其他郡縣悉命弘靖統之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Muzong wished quickly to gain Fanyang; the chief ministers Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying also did not plan for the long term but only wished to enlarge what Hongjing received, and could not reduce his commissioner establishment; only Ying and Mo two prefectures were permitted to have observation commissioners, and all other commanderies and counties were ordered under Hongjing's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Muzong wished quickly to gain Fanyang; chief ministers Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying did not plan long-term but only wished to enlarge Hongjing's grant and could not reduce his establishment; only Ying and Mo received observation commissioners, and all other counties were placed under Hongjing.

sentences.zh: 時總所薦將校，又俱在京師旅舍中，久而不問。

translations.literal: At that time the generals Zong had recommended were all in lodging houses in the capital and long went unasked after.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the generals Zong had recommended were all in capital lodging houses and long went unasked after.

sentences.zh: 如硃克融輩，僅至假衣丐食，日詣中書求官，不勝其困。

translations.literal: Men such as Zhu Kerong barely reached borrowing clothes and begging food, daily going to the Secretariat to seek office, unable to bear their hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Zhu Kerong barely reached borrowing clothes and begging food, daily going to the Secretariat to seek office, unable to bear their hardship.

sentences.zh: 及除弘靖，又命悉還本軍。

translations.literal: When Hongjing was appointed, an order also commanded all to return to their original armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjing was appointed, an order also commanded all to return to their original armies.

sentences.zh: 克融輩雖得復歸，皆深懷觖望，其後果為叛亂。

translations.literal: Although Kerong and the others were able to return, all deeply harbored resentment, and afterward they indeed raised rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Although Kerong and the others returned, all deeply resented it, and afterward they indeed rebelled.

sentences.zh: 總既以土地歸國，授其弟約及男等一十一人，領郡符，加命服者五人，升朝班，佐宿衛者六人。

translations.literal: When Zong had returned his territory to the empire, his younger brother Yue and eleven sons and others were granted prefectural tally slips; five received ceremonial robes and entered court ranks; six served as palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong had returned his territory, his younger brother Yue and eleven sons received prefectural appointments; five received ceremonial robes and entered court ranks; six served as palace guards.

sentences.zh: 程日華，定州安喜人，本單名華。

translations.literal: Cheng Rihua was a man of Anxi in Ding prefecture; originally his single name was Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Rihua was from Anxi in Ding prefecture; originally his single name was Hua.

sentences.zh: 父元皓，事安祿山為帳下將，從陷兩京，頗稱勇力，史思明時為定州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yuanhao served An Lushan as a commander under his tent, followed in capturing the two capitals, was known for courage and strength, and under Shi Siming was governor of Ding prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanhao served An Lushan as a tent commander, followed in capturing the two capitals, was known for courage, and under Shi Siming was governor of Ding prefecture.

sentences.zh: 華少事本軍，為張孝忠牙將。

translations.literal: Hua in youth served the home army and was a yamen officer under Zhang Xiaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Hua in youth served the home army and was a yamen officer under Zhang Xiaozhong.

sentences.zh: 初，李寶臣授恆州節度，吞削籓鄰，有恆、冀、深、趙、易、定、滄、德等八州。

translations.literal: At first, when Li Baochen was granted Heng prefecture as military governor, he swallowed and cut down neighboring commands and held eight prefectures: Heng, Ji, Shen, Zhao, Yi, Ding, Cang, and De.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Li Baochen was granted Hengzhou as governor, he swallowed neighboring commands and held eight prefectures: Heng, Ji, Shen, Zhao, Yi, Ding, Cang, and De.

sentences.zh: 寶臣既卒，惟嶽拒朝命，以圖繼襲。

translations.literal: When Baochen died, Weiyue defied the court's orders, intending to succeed by inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: When Baochen died, Weiyue defied court orders, intending to succeed by inheritance.

sentences.zh: 寶臣部將張孝忠以定州歸國，授成德軍節度使，令與硃滔討惟嶽。

translations.literal: Baochen's officer Zhang Xiaozhong returned Ding prefecture to the empire and was appointed military governor of the Chengde army and ordered with Zhu Tao to attack Weiyue.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen's officer Zhang Xiaozhong returned Dingzhou to the empire and was appointed Chengde governor and ordered with Zhu Tao to attack Weiyue.

sentences.zh: 及惟嶽誅，朝廷以恆、冀授王武俊，深、趙授康日知，易、定、滄授張孝忠，分為三帥。

translations.literal: When Weiyue was executed, the court granted Heng and Ji to Wang Wujun, Shen and Zhao to Kang Rizhi, and Yi, Ding, and Cang to Zhang Xiaozhong, dividing them among three commanders.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiyue was executed, the court granted Heng and Ji to Wang Wujun, Shen and Zhao to Kang Rizhi, and Yi, Ding, and Cang to Zhang Xiaozhong, dividing them among three commanders.

sentences.zh: 時惟嶽將李固烈守滄州，孝忠令華詣固烈交郡。

translations.literal: At that time Weiyue's officer Li Gulei held Cang prefecture; Xiaozhong ordered Hua to go to Gulei to transfer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Weiyue's officer Li Gulei held Cangzhou; Xiaozhong ordered Hua to go to Gulei to transfer the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 固烈將歸真定，悉取滄州府藏，累乘而還。

translations.literal: Gulei was about to return to Zhending and took all Cang prefecture's treasury stores, loading cart upon cart in returning.
translations.idiomatic: Gulei was about to return to Zhending and took all Cangzhou's treasury stores, loading cart upon cart.

sentences.zh: 軍人怒，殺固烈，皆奪其財，相與詣華曰：「李使君貪鄙而死，軍州請押牙權領。」

translations.literal: The soldiers were angry, killed Gulei, and all seized his property; together they went to Hua and said, "Commissioner Li was greedy and base and has died; the army and prefecture ask the yamen adjutant to take charge provisionally."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were angry, killed Gulei, and seized his property; together they went to Hua and said, "Commissioner Li was greedy and base and has died; the army and prefecture ask the yamen adjutant to take charge provisionally."

sentences.zh: 不獲已，從之。

translations.literal: Unable to refuse, he consented.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse, he consented.

sentences.zh: 孝忠因授華知滄州事。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong thereupon appointed Hua to manage Cang prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong thereupon appointed Hua to manage Cang prefecture affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，硃滔合武俊謀叛，滄、定往來艱阻，二盜遂欲取滄州，多遣人遊說，又加兵攻圍，華俱不聽從，乘城自固。

translations.literal: Before long Zhu Tao joined Wujun in plotting rebellion; travel between Cang and Ding was difficult, and the two rebels then wished to take Cang prefecture; they sent many men to persuade him and also added troops in siege; Hua would not heed any of it and manned the walls to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhu Tao joined Wujun in plotting rebellion; travel between Cang and Ding was difficult, and the two rebels wished to take Cangzhou; they sent many persuaders and besieged with troops; Hua would not heed any of it and manned the walls.

sentences.zh: 久之，錄事參軍李宇為華謀曰：「使君受圍累年，張尚書不能致援，論功獻捷，須至中山，所謂勞而無功者也。

translations.literal: After a long time, the recording secretary Li Yu advised Hua, saying, "My lord has been besieged for years; Minister Zhang cannot bring relief; to report merit and present victory one must reach Zhongshan—this is what is called labor without result.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, recording secretary Li Yu advised Hua, saying, "My lord has been besieged for years; Minister Zhang cannot bring relief; to report merit and present victory one must reach Zhongshan—this is labor without result.

sentences.zh: 請為足下至京師，自以一州為使。」

translations.literal: I ask to go to the capital on your behalf and offer this one prefecture as a commission."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to go to the capital on your behalf and offer this one prefecture as a commission."

sentences.zh: 華即遣之。

translations.literal: Hua immediately dispatched him.
translations.idiomatic: Hua immediately dispatched him.

sentences.zh: 宇入闕，備陳華當二盜之間，疲於矢石。

translations.literal: Yu entered court and fully set forth how Hua stood between the two rebels, weary under arrows and stones.
translations.idiomatic: Yu entered court and fully set forth how Hua stood between the two rebels, weary under arrows and stones.

sentences.zh: 德宗深嘉之，拜華御史中丞、滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong deeply commended this and appointed Hua vice censor-in-chief and governor of Cang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong deeply commended this and appointed Hua vice censor-in-chief and governor of Cang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復置橫海軍，以華為使。

translations.literal: The Henghai army was restored and Hua was made its commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Henghai army was restored and Hua was made its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋加工部尚書、御史大夫，賜名日華，仍歲給義武軍糧餉數萬。

translations.literal: He was soon further made minister of works and chief censor; he was granted the name Rihua and still received yearly supplies of Yiwu army grain in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further made minister of works and chief censor; he was granted the name Rihua and still received yearly Yiwu army grain supplies in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 自是別為一使，孝忠唯有易、定二州而已。

translations.literal: From this it became a separate command; Xiaozhong had only Yi and Ding two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: From this it became a separate command; Xiaozhong had only Yi and Ding two prefectures.

sentences.zh: 武俊遣人說華歸己，華曰：「相公欲敝邑仍舊隸恆州，且借騎二百以抗賊，俟道路通即從命。」

translations.literal: Wujun sent someone to persuade Hua to return to him; Hua said, "My lord wishes our humble district again to be subordinate to Heng prefecture; lend us two hundred horsemen to resist the rebels, and once the roads are open we shall obey."
translations.idiomatic: Wujun sent someone to persuade Hua to return to him; Hua said, "My lord wishes our humble district again to be subordinate to Heng prefecture; lend us two hundred horsemen to resist the rebels, and once the roads are open we shall obey."

sentences.zh: 武俊喜，即以二百騎助之。

translations.literal: Wujun was pleased and sent two hundred horsemen to help.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was pleased and sent two hundred horsemen to help.

sentences.zh: 華乃留其馬，遣人皆還。

translations.literal: Hua then kept their horses and sent the men all back.
translations.idiomatic: Hua then kept their horses and sent the men all back.

sentences.zh: 武俊怒其背約，又以硃滔方攻圍，慮為所有而止。

translations.literal: Wujun was angry at his breach of covenant, but because Zhu Tao was then besieging he feared Hua would be taken and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was angry at the breach of covenant, but because Zhu Tao was then besieging he feared Hua would be taken and stopped.

sentences.zh: 及武俊歸國，河朔無事，日華即遣所留馬還武俊，別陳珍幣謝過，武俊歡然而釋。

translations.literal: When Wujun returned to the empire and the Hebei region was without trouble, Rihua sent back the horses he had kept and separately presented precious gifts in apology; Wujun gladly released his anger.
translations.idiomatic: When Wujun returned to the empire and Hebei was tranquil, Rihua returned the horses he had kept and presented precious gifts in apology; Wujun gladly released his anger.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年卒，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan he died and was posthumously made minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 4 he died and was posthumously made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 子懷直。

translations.literal: His son Huaizhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaizhi.

sentences.zh: 懷直習河朔事，父卒，自知留後事。

translations.literal: Huaizhi was versed in Hebei affairs; when his father died he himself took charge of provisional affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhi knew Hebei affairs; when his father died he himself took charge of provisional affairs.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉父之忠，起復授檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫，升橫海軍為節度，以懷直為留後。

translations.literal: The court commended his father's loyalty and appointed him on mourning leave as acting minister of works and concurrent chief censor; the Henghai army was raised to a military governorship and Huaizhi was made acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended his father's loyalty and appointed him on mourning leave as acting minister of works and concurrent chief censor; Henghai was raised to a governorship and Huaizhi was made acting governor.

sentences.zh: 又於弓高縣置景州，管東光、景城二縣，以為屬郡。

translations.literal: Jing prefecture was also established at Gonggao county to administer Dongguang and Jingcheng two counties as subordinate commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Jing prefecture was also established at Gonggao county to administer Dongguang and Jingcheng counties as subordinate commanderies.

sentences.zh: 累加至檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to acting right vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to acting right vice minister.

sentences.zh: 五年，起復正授節度觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was formally appointed on mourning leave as military governor and observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was formally appointed on mourning leave as governor and observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 懷直荒於畋獵，數日方還，不恤軍政，軍士不勝寒餒。

translations.literal: Huaizhi was idle in hunting; several days would pass before he returned and he did not care for military administration; the soldiers could not bear cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhi was idle in hunting; days would pass before he returned and he neglected military administration; the soldiers could not bear cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 其帳下將從父兄懷信因眾怒閉門不內，懷直因來朝覲，貞元九年也。

translations.literal: His tent officer Huaixin, his father's younger brother's son, taking advantage of popular anger, closed the gates and would not admit him; Huaizhi therefore came to court audience—in the ninth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His tent officer Huaixin, his father's cousin, exploiting popular anger, closed the gates and would not admit him; Huaizhi therefore came to court—in Zhenyuan 9.

sentences.zh: 德宗優容之，依前檢校右僕射，兼龍武統軍，賜安業裏甲第，妓女一人。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong indulged him and restored him as acting right vice minister and concurrent commander of the Longwu army; he was granted a mansion in Anye Lane and one courtesan.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong indulged him and restored him as acting right vice minister and concurrent Longwu commander; he was granted a mansion in Anye Lane and one courtesan.

sentences.zh: 既而懷信死，懷直子執恭知留後事，乃遣懷直歸滄州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Huaixin died; Huaizhi's son Zhigong managed provisional affairs and then sent Huaizhi back to Cang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huaixin died; Huaizhi's son Zhigong managed provisional affairs and sent Huaizhi back to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十六年卒，年四十九，廢朝一日，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died at forty-nine; court was suspended one day and he was posthumously made chief administrator of Yang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died at forty-nine; court was suspended one day and he was posthumously made chief administrator of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 執恭代襲父位，朝廷因而授之。

translations.literal: Zhigong succeeded his father in office and the court thereupon appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigong succeeded his father and the court appointed him.

sentences.zh: 元和六年入朝，憲宗禮遇遣之，加尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he entered court; Emperor Xianzong received him with ritual and sent him back, further making him left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 6 he entered court; Xianzong received him with ritual and sent him back, further making him left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 嘗夢滄州衙門樓額悉帖「權」字，遂奏請改名權。

translations.literal: He once dreamed that the plaque of the Cang prefecture yamen gate tower was entirely pasted with the character 'Quan'; he therefore memorialized asking to change his name to Quan.
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed the Cangzhou yamen gate plaque was entirely pasted with the character 'Quan'; he memorialized asking to change his name to Quan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，淮西賊平，籓方惕息，權以父子世襲如三鎮事例，心不自安，乃請入朝。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the Huaixi rebels were pacified and frontier commands were subdued, Quan, like the three-circuit precedent of father and son succeeding by inheritance, was ill at ease in heart and asked to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when Huaixi was pacified and frontier commands were subdued, Quan, like the three-circuit precedent of hereditary succession, was ill at ease and asked to enter court.

sentences.zh: 十三年，至京師，表辭戎帥，因命華州刺史鄭權代之，以靖安裏私第側狹，賜地二十畝，令廣其居。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he reached the capital, submitted a memorial declining military command, and was ordered replaced by Hua prefecture governor Zheng Quan; because his private residence beside Jing'an Lane was narrow, twenty mu of land were granted to enlarge his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he reached the capital, declined military command, and was replaced by Hua prefecture governor Zheng Quan; because his Jing'an Lane residence was narrow, twenty mu were granted to enlarge it.

sentences.zh: 尋遷檢校司空、邠州刺史、邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to acting chief minister, governor of Bin prefecture, and military governor of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to acting chief minister, Binzhou governor, and Binning governor.

sentences.zh: 十四年十一月卒，贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year he died and was posthumously made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year he died and was posthumously made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 權兄弟子侄在朝列宿衛者三十余人。

translations.literal: Quan's brothers, sons, and nephews in court ranks and palace guard numbered more than thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's brothers, sons, and nephews in court ranks and palace guard numbered more than thirty.

sentences.zh: 李全略者，本姓王，名日簡。

translations.literal: Li Quanlue originally had the surname Wang and the name Rijian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quanlue originally had the surname Wang and the name Rijian.

sentences.zh: 為鎮州小將，事王武俊。

translations.literal: He was a junior officer of Zhen prefecture and served Wang Wujun.
translations.idiomatic: He was a junior officer of Zhenzhou and served Wang Wujun.

sentences.zh: 元和中，節度使王承宗沒，軍情不安，自拔歸朝，授代州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, when military governor Wang Chengzong died army sentiment was unsettled; he on his own initiative returned to the empire and was appointed governor of Dai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era, when governor Wang Chengzong died army sentiment was unsettled; he returned to the empire on his own and was appointed Daizhou governor.

sentences.zh: 及長慶初，鎮州軍亂，殺田弘正；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, the Zhen prefecture army mutinied and killed Tian Hongzheng;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Changqing, the Zhenzhou army mutinied and killed Tian Hongzheng;

sentences.zh: 穆宗為之旰食，以日簡嘗為鎮將，召問其計。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong, troubled over it, because Rijian had once been an officer of Zhen, summoned him and asked his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong, troubled over it, because Rijian had once been a Zhen officer, summoned him and asked his plan.

sentences.zh: 日簡遂於御前極言利害，兼願有以自效，因授德州刺史，經略其事。

translations.literal: Rijian then before the throne fully set forth advantage and harm and also expressed willingness to serve with merit; he was therefore appointed governor of De prefecture to manage the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Rijian before the throne fully set forth advantage and harm and expressed willingness to serve; he was appointed Dezhou governor to manage the affair.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢拜橫海軍節度使，賜姓李氏，名全略，以崇樹之。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to military governor of the Henghai army; he was granted the surname Li and the name Quanlue, to honor and establish him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to Henghai governor; he was granted the surname Li and the name Quanlue, to honor and establish him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，令子同捷入侍，兼進錢千萬。

translations.literal: Before long he sent his son Tongjie to attend court and also presented ten million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he sent his son Tongjie to attend court and also presented ten million in cash.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，同捷歸覲，乃奏請授滄州長史、知州事，兼主中軍兵馬；

translations.literal: After a year Tongjie returned to visit his parents; he then memorialized asking that Tongjie be appointed chief administrator of Cang prefecture with control of prefecture affairs and command of the central army and horse forces;
translations.idiomatic: After a year Tongjie returned to visit his parents; he memorialized asking that Tongjie be appointed Cangzhou chief administrator with control of prefecture affairs and command of the central army;

sentences.zh: 朝廷初不之許，後慮其有奇策，將副經略之旨，遂從之。

translations.literal: at first the court did not assent; later, fearing he had a special stratagem to assist the overall plan of the campaign, it followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: at first the court did not assent; later, fearing he had a special stratagem, it followed his request.

sentences.zh: 及得請，全略乃陰結軍士，潛為久計，外示忠順，內畜奸謀。

translations.literal: When he obtained his request, Quanlue secretly won over the soldiers and secretly made long-term plans, outwardly showing loyal submission while inwardly harboring treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: When he obtained his request, Quanlue secretly won over the soldiers and made long-term plans, outwardly showing loyal submission while inwardly harboring treachery.

sentences.zh: 棣州刺史王稷善撫眾，且得其心，全略忌而殺之，仍孥戮其屬。

translations.literal: Di prefecture governor Wang Ji was good at comforting the masses and had won their hearts; Quanlue envied and killed him and still exterminated his dependents.
translations.idiomatic: Di prefecture governor Wang Ji was good at comforting the masses and had won their hearts; Quanlue envied and killed him and exterminated his dependents.

sentences.zh: 凡所為事，大率類此。

translations.literal: In general what he did was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: In general what he did was mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年四月卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Baoli he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Baoli 2 he died.

sentences.zh: 子同捷，初為副大使，居喪，擅領留後事，仍重賂籓鄰以求纘襲，朝廷知其所為，經年不問。

translations.literal: His son Tongjie at first was deputy commissioner; during mourning he on his own took provisional affairs and still heavily bribed neighboring commands to seek succession; the court knew what he was doing and for a full year did not inquire.
